Capability Maturity Model Integration (CMMI) 
1. Introduction 
CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration) is a process improvement framework 
used to evaluate and improve the quality, efficiency, and maturity of software 
development processes in an organization.
creator: Microsoft® Word 2024
author: nitiny2k17@gmail.com

text:
Introduction 
CMMI (Capability Maturity Model Integration) is a process improvement framework 
used to evaluate and improve the quality, efficiency, and maturity of software 
development processes in an organization. It helps organizations: 
• 
Develop high-quality software 
• 
Improve process consistency 
• 
Reduce project risks 
• 
Meet customer requirements effectively 
 
2.
creator: Microsoft® Word 2024
author: nitiny2k17@gmail.com

text:
It helps organizations: 
• 
Develop high-quality software 
• 
Improve process consistency 
• 
Reduce project risks 
• 
Meet customer requirements effectively 
 
2. CMMI Maturity Levels 
CMMI defines five maturity levels that indicate the capability of an organization’s 
processes: 
Level 1 – Initial 
• 
Processes are ad hoc and unpredictable 
• 
No standardized procedures 
• 
Success depends on individual effort 
Level 2 – Managed 
• 
Basic project management practices are established 
• 
Requirements, schedules, and costs are planned and tracked 
• 
Projects are better controlled 
Level 3 – Defined 
• 
Organization-wide standard processes are established 
• 
Processes are well documented and understood 
• 
Standardization across projects 
Level 4 – Quantitatively Managed 
• 
Processes are measured and controlled using metrics 
• 
Data-driven decision making
creator: Microsoft® Word 2024
author: nitiny2k17@gmail.com

text:
• 
Performance is predictable 
Level 5 – Optimizing 
• 
Focus on continuous process improvement 
• 
Emphasis on defect prevention and innovation 
• 
Ongoing improvement through feedback and analysis
